transform_notes: SAP's real key is the composite (Company Code + Fiscal Year + Document Number / BELNR), normally system-assigned from a number range. Keep Journal_Entry_ID only as a migration cross-reference attribute.
Resolve via Foundation>Companies lookup before load.

Verified against the source: this header value always equals the Account_ID of that entry's own Line_Number=1 row in General Ledger (checked across sample entries). A real journal entry posts to multiple accounts -- the true per-line accounts are already captured on the General Ledger rows (see journal_entries -> general_ledger_field_mapping.csv). Standard BKPF has no single-account header field; don't carry this one forward, it's a denormalization artifact of the source design.

SAP normally assigns BELNR internally from a number range. Preserving the human-readable legacy number requires external number range assignment for the document type in the target system; otherwise it survives only as a cross-reference attribute -- same pattern as Order_Number in the Sales Orders example.
The date on the source document itself, distinct from Posted_At below (posting date).
Resolve via Foundation>Accounting Periods lookup to the target fiscal year + period; the period is normally derived from the posting date, but an explicit override is supported (BKPF-MONAT).

Maps to a configured document type (e.g. distinct types for system-generated postings vs. manual entries). 'Recurring' specifically may warrant SAP's Recurring Entry functionality (transaction FBD1) rather than a plain document-type flag -- confirm with the target system's document type catalog.
Points back to the originating business document (e.g. the customer invoice this entry was generated from).

Not a BKPF/ACDOCA field. A balanced document's total debit equals total credit by construction (SAP will not post an unbalanced document) and is simply the sum of the debit-side General Ledger lines -- don't load this as a field, use it as a pre-load validation check instead (see worked-example notes).
Same as Debit_Total -- derived/validation value, not a stored field.

BKPF stores the entering SAP username (CHAR(12)), not a numeric user ID. This column appears to overlap conceptually with Created_By_User_ID below -- confirm with the business which one is authoritative (the actual data-entry preparer vs. a generic audit 'created by') before deciding what maps here.

Consistent with Foundation>Approval Requests: document release/approval is rebuilt via SAP's release/workflow configuration in the target system, not carried as a flat field. Standard BKPF has no 'approved by' column.

All 257 source entries are 'Posted', so this table only ever needs the BKPF target. If the source later includes not-yet-posted entries, those route to VBKPF (parked document header) instead -- in SAP, which table the document lives in IS the status, not a field value on one table.

Maps the date portion to BUDAT (Posting Date). The time-of-day is only available as a technical system timestamp (entry time), not a business field -- don't expect to preserve it as cleanly as the date.
Every accounting document stamps its own creation metadata automatically -- not loaded as source data.
Posted FI documents are normally immutable (reversed, not edited) -- tracked via change documents where changes are even possible. Not loaded as source data.

Captured automatically as the posting SAP user. See the Prepared_By_User_ID note above -- clarify with the business whether this or Prepared_By_User_ID is the field actually worth preserving as a cross-reference attribute; loading both is probably redundant.
